t3302.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records ʿAbdallāh ibn Dhakwān al-Qurashī, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Madanī, known as Abū al-Zinād, as trustworthy and a jurist, of the fifth generation; he died in 30, or later it is said.
as: Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
ثقة، فقيه، صالح الحديث، صاحب سنة، وهو ممن تقوم به الحجة إذا روى عنه الثقات.
Trustworthy, a jurist, sound in hadith and an adherent of the Sunnah. His transmission serves as evidence when trustworthy people report from him.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
Commander of the Faithful in hadith.
وهو فوق العلاء بن عبد الرحمن، وفوق سهيل بن أبي صالح، وفوق محمد بن عمرو.
He ranks above al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Suhayl ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ and Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
أن أبا الزناد أعلم من ربيعة
Abū al-Zinād was more learned than Rabīʿah.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
ابن أبو مريم, quoted by al-Mizzī
An authority, in Ibn Abī Maryam’s version of Ibn Maʿīn’s verdict.
ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī, quoted by al-Mizzī
لم يكن بالمدينة بعد كبار التابعين أعلم من ابن شهاب، ويحيى بن سعيد الأنصاري، وأبي الزناد، وبكير بن عبد الله بن الأشج.
After the senior Successors, no one in Medina was more learned than Ibn Shihāb, Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Anṣārī, Abū al-Zinād and Bukayr ibn ʿAbd Allāh.
مدني، تابعي، ثقة، سمع من أنس بن مالك.
A Medinan Successor, trustworthy. He heard Anas ibn Mālik.
وأصح أسانيد أبي هريرة: أبو الزناد، عن الأعرج، عن أبي هريرة.
The soundest chain for Abū Hurayrah is Abū al-Zinād from al-Aʿraj from Abū Hurayrah.
Abū al-Zinād was the better jurist of the two.
وكان ثقة، كثير الحديث، فصيحا، بصيرا بالعربية، عاما، عاقلا.
He was trustworthy, prolific in hadith, eloquent, knowledgeable in Arabic and judicious.
وكان ثقة كثير الحديث. فصيحا بصيرا بالعربية عالما عاقلا
He was trustworthy and prolific in hadith, eloquent and knowledgeable in Arabic, learned and judicious.

t7333.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Hilāl ibn Abī Ḥumayd al-Juhanī, Abū al-Jahm al-Ṣayrafī al-Wazzān al-Kūfī, as trustworthy, of the sixth generation, noting disagreement over his father's name and kunya.

t7463.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records al-Walīd ibn Abī Hishām Ziyād, brother of Hishām Abī al-Miqdām, al-Madanī, as ṣadūq, of the sixth generation.

t7489.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Wuhayb ibn al-Ward al-Qurashī, Abū ʿUthmān or Abū Umayya al-Makkī, as trustworthy and devout, of the leading seventh generation; some say his name is ʿAbd al-Wahhāb.

t7517.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Yaḥyā ibn Abī Bukayr al-Nakhaʿī al-Kūfī as obscure, of the tenth generation, who died in the year 30 AH.

t7580.bio: Ibn Ḥajar calls Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, al-Makhzūmī al-Miṣrī, trustworthy in al-Layth, though his hearing from Mālik was criticized; of the senior tenth generation, he died in 231 aged seventy-seven.
as: They criticized his hearing from Mālik.
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
يكتب حديثه ولا يحتج به، وكان يفهم هذا الشأن.
His reports can be written but are insufficient as proof. He understood hadith.
ضعيف. وقال في موضع آخر: ليس بثقة.
Al-Nasāʾī called him weak, and elsewhere said he was not trustworthy.
Ibn Ḥibbān listed him among trustworthy transmitters.
